summary: Found while diagnosing a user-reported bench failure that looked like their own last-frame-only edit. It was not. ComfyUI f8a3fd9d (2026-07-25) converted LatentUpscaleModelLoader's return to a ModelPatcher/ModelPatcherDynamic; KJNodes' OuterSampleCallbackWrapper still called latent_upscale_model.to(device), and neither patcher class defines .to - proven by hasattr against the ENGINE's own python. Every shipped LTX graph (all 12) wires that optional input, so the whole LTX fleet dies at the stage-1 sampler on 0.30.x. The engine ships ComfyUI 0.30.0 which already contains the breaking commit, and KJNodes 1.4.7 without the fix, so this is a product regression from the H3 engine bump, not a bench-only problem. kijai fixed it in 827fe6e (2026-07-28) with the message 'Update ltxv_nodes.py' - the _unwrap_upscale_model helper. Pin bumped 7f43f2c -> 35e5956 (upstream head, 38 commits, no requirements change, neither ImageResizeKJv2 nor LTX2SamplingPreviewOverride renamed). PROVEN LIVE on the bench: the exact failing prompt re-queued after the bump ran the whole graph to completion in 124s.

CORRECTION, and it makes the card worse. The first write blamed the H3 engine bump (0.29.2 -> 0.30.0) and said the breakage was unnoticed because nobody had run LTX since. Both were wrong, and the user was right that a ComfyUI bump did it - just an earlier one. Checked at the release tags: the loader returns a patcher from v0.29.0 (tagged 2026-07-28) and NOT in v0.28.0, and our engine pin crossed v0.28.0 -> v0.29.2 on 2026-07-31 in commit e2c2b4d6. Worse, it is not internal: v1.3.0 (published 2026-08-01) and v1.3.1 (2026-08-02) BOTH pin comfyui core v0.29.2 with kjnodes 7f43f2c, so every user on the current public release has had a completely dead LTX for about six days. That reclassifies this from an unreleased-changelog line to a shipped regression and a hotfix candidate. Lesson recorded: 'git tag --contains' answers by topology and said the commit was in v0.29.0-v0.30.2 without telling me our own pin history - reading the file AT each tag plus the repo's own node_lock history is what actually dated it.

Attention healed at close-out. It still asked for a local engine restart and a Pod rebuild; the local half is now confirmed by the user (LTX i2v ops all pass locally) and the Pod image is already at v0.20.0-dev on ComfyUI 0.30.0. The single remaining proof is the MPI-467 smoke matrix, so this card closes on smoke-evidence.json rather than on another local check.

LTX is PROVEN ALIVE on the shipped engine. The card's own bar was 'close this on smoke-evidence.json, not another local check', and the third matrix reached the GPU stage for the first time: ltx-23-balanced/t2v_ms PASS 78s 1 media, i2v_ms PASS 42s 2 media, on L4 orxp87067tddah with gate 7 clear (Pod image built from 0.30.0, matches node_lock). Real wall-clock and real media, not the 4s no-op shape that let a dead graph read green. The LOCAL half was user-confirmed 2026-08-08. The matrix's one remaining failure is minimax-h3/t2v_ms = MPI-501, unrelated to LTX and tracked on MPI-467.
